metadata.title: External / Federated Integration SSPP
metadata.remarks: System Security and Privacy Plan defining trust, governance, and lifecycle constraints for external and federated system-to-system integrations involving third-party organizations.

import-profile.remarks: This SSPP inherits all Secure-Integration Platform trust semantics and introduces stricter constraints for integrations with external or federated entities.

system-characteristics.system-description: External or Federated Integration environments enable system-to-system interactions across organizational boundaries. These integrations operate under reduced trust assumptions, explicit contractual controls, strict lifecycle governance, and elevated monitoring.

props.name: integration-trust-tier
props.remarks: Indicates integrations that cross institutional or organizational trust boundaries.

props.name: trust-assumption
props.remarks: External systems are treated as untrusted by default and must continuously earn trust through explicit signals.

props.name: identity-model
props.remarks: Federated non-human identities must be explicitly bound, scoped, and attributable.

props.name: authorization-scope
props.remarks: External integrations are authorized for narrowly scoped, contractually defined purposes only.

props.name: replay-policy
props.remarks: Replay of external integration data is prohibited unless explicitly approved and time-bound.

props.name: retention-tolerance
props.remarks: Retention of externally sourced integration data is minimized to reduce downstream risk.

props.name: fan-out-policy
props.remarks: External data must not be fan-out distributed without explicit approval.

props.name: lifecycle-policy
props.remarks: External integrations require explicit onboarding, periodic re-approval, and deterministic revocation.

props.name: business-authorization
props.remarks: External integration trust signals must never be interpreted as business or policy authorization.

system-implementation.remarks: External / Federated Integration environments rely on the full Secure-Integration signal stack with reduced trust assumptions and elevated governance. This SSPP does not define contractual terms, legal agreements, or remediation actions.

roles.title: External Integration Architecture
roles.remarks: Defines architectural patterns and constraints for federated and third-party integrations.

roles.title: External Integration Governance
roles.remarks: Approves onboarding, reauthorization, trust scope, and termination of external integrations.

roles.title: External Integration Operations
roles.remarks: Operates externally facing integration platforms under strict trust and monitoring constraints.

roles.title: External Integration Security Monitoring
roles.remarks: Monitors external integration traffic, trust degradation, replay attempts, and lifecycle violations.

control-implementation.remarks: Controls are satisfied through inheritance from Secure-Integration patterns and stricter interpretation of trust signals. This SSPP introduces no new control implementations.
